results.title: Agenda Hero vs Text to Calendar (2026)
results.content:
## What Agenda Hero does

Agenda Hero markets itself as a platform that "converts anything to calendar events." Its core feature is Agenda Hero Magic: you type, paste, snap a photo, or upload a screenshot or PDF, and the AI parses it into a structured event with the title, date, time, location, description, and even an emoji filled in. You can edit any field afterward, and you refine results with a chat-style prompt. It handles multiple events from a single input (for example, pasting a soccer schedule or a newsletter) and supports recurring events including daily, weekly, every-other-week, monthly, and annual patterns. You can specify a start and end time ("11am to 1pm") or a start plus duration ("2pm for 90 minutes"). [...] If you're comparing Agenda Hero with Text to Calendar, the short answer is this: both use AI to turn messy text into calendar events, but they aim at different jobs. Agenda Hero is a full calendar product with a side panel, shareable "Magic Pages," and a directory of pre-built academic calendars; it exports to Google, Apple, and Outlook. Text to Calendar is a lightweight browser extension that lives where you already read text, turning a highlight into a Google Calendar or Outlook event with a right-click and no separate app to open. If you want a calendar destination and curated school schedules, Agenda Hero is the better fit. If you just want the fastest path from selected text to a saved event, Text to Calendar wins. Here is the honest breakdown.

## What Agenda Hero does [...] Both tools parse text into events well, so the decision comes down to where you want the work to happen. Agenda Hero is a destination — a side panel, shareable Magic Pages, image/PDF parsing, and a ready-made academic-calendar library. If you publish calendars or wrangle PDFs and photos, it's worth the $30/year Plus plan. Text to Calendar is a shortcut — it stays out of the way until you highlight text, then turns that highlight into a Google or Outlook event without a second app. If you mostly create events from text you're already reading, and especially if you're on Outlook, Text to Calendar is the faster, cheaper way to get there. Many people will reasonably keep both: Agenda Hero for big imports and shared calendars, Text to Calendar for the dozens of small "add this to my calendar"
